stocks:CVX.recent: The one story about its own business was a disclosure question: its Nigerian unit and Shell's reported identical methane emissions for 2022. Nothing in that accounts for the share's rise.

stocks:AAPL.standing: Shares of the Cupertino maker of the iPhone, Mac and iPad, one of the world's most valuable listed companies. The iPhone earns most of its revenue, and its products are assembled largely in China on chips made in Taiwan.
stocks:AAPL.recent: Apple put its M6 chip in a new MacBook Pro and iMac, bringing a touchscreen and OLED to the Mac and claiming 24 hours of battery from $1,999. Its foldable iPhone, meanwhile, drew reports of growing pains and a crease. Alibaba's Qwen is also coming to Chinese iPhones through Apple Intelligence, news that arrived after the chart's last close.

stocks:ISP.MI.standing: Italy's largest bank by assets, listed in Milan, with a dominant share of the country's retail deposits and a big book of Italian government bonds, so its shares move with Italian sovereign risk.
stocks:ISP.MI.recent: The ECB gave Intesa Sanpaolo authorisation to take over Monte dei Paschi, clearing the way for a €32 billion bid. That approval came only this week, after the shares had already slid, and nothing else in the input explains the earlier fall.

stocks:002415.SZ.standing: The world's largest maker of video-surveillance cameras, listed in Shenzhen and controlled by state-owned CETC. US sanctions and Western bans on its gear in government sites limit what it can sell abroad.

stocks:BMPS.MI.standing: The Siena lender founded in 1472, the oldest bank still operating. The Italian state rescued it in 2017, and its fate has since been a test of how far Italy's banks will consolidate.
stocks:BMPS.MI.recent: The ECB authorised Intesa Sanpaolo to take over Monte dei Paschi, which clears Italy's largest bank to bid €32 billion for the Siena lender. The approval came at the end of the period, and nothing reported before it accounts for the share's earlier fall.

stocks:002236.SZ.standing: One of China's two largest makers of surveillance cameras and video systems, based in Hangzhou. US export blacklisting and an FCC equipment ban shut it out of American markets, so its sales lean on China and emerging markets.

stocks:000063.SZ.standing: China's second-largest telecom equipment maker after Huawei, based in Shenzhen and listed there and in Hong Kong. A 2018 US export ban nearly shut it down, so its shares move on Washington's rules on chips.

stocks:COIN.standing: The largest US cryptocurrency exchange, listed on Nasdaq. Most of its revenue comes from trading fees and custody, so its shares move with crypto prices and how much people trade.
stocks:COIN.recent: A vendor breach exposed the contact details of a "small subset" of Coinbase customers, but that report came after the last close on this chart. Nothing else carried here concerns Coinbase's own business, so none of it accounts for the fall in the share price.

stocks:AMPL.standing: Amplitude sells product-analytics software that records how people use apps and websites, so companies can see which features keep customers. Its subscription revenue rises and falls with corporate software budgets.

stocks:RELIANCE.NS.standing: India's most valuable company, controlled by Mukesh Ambani: the world's largest refining complex at Jamnagar, the Jio telecom network and a vast retail chain. Its shares move with refining margins and Indian consumer demand.
stocks:RELIANCE.NS.recent: Reliance listed Jio Platforms in India's largest initial public offering: a Rs 30,188 crore issue drew Rs 7.4 lakh crore in bids, and the unit is now the second most valued Indian firm. Rubio, meanwhile, pressed India's refineries to process more Venezuelan crude. Neither report explains the parent's share price.

stocks:3988.HK.standing: One of China's four large state-owned commercial banks, and the most international of them: it clears offshore yuan in Hong Kong and other centres, so its shares carry both Beijing's credit policy and the yuan's spread abroad.
stocks:3988.HK.recent: Bank of China's 2 billion yuan Yulan bond debuted in Dubai and drew 5 times demand, part of Beijing's push for yuan-denominated assets. The sale shows appetite for the bank's debt abroad, but it does not account for the share price, and nothing else in the fortnight's news about the bank does either.

stocks:ADANIENT.NS.standing: The flagship listed company of India's Adani Group, which starts new businesses such as airports, mining, roads and copper before spinning them off. Its share price is the market's read on the whole conglomerate's debt and governance.
stocks:ADANIENT.NS.recent: Adani Enterprises returned to profit in its latest quarter on its copper, renewables and airports units, and copper now supplies nearly 40% of its revenue. The results arrived after the share's slide, and nothing reported about the company this month accounts for the fall.

stocks:TTE.standing: France's largest oil and gas company, with production across Africa, the Middle East and the North Sea and one of the world's biggest LNG portfolios. Its share moves with crude and gas prices and refining margins.

stocks:DKNG.standing: A Boston-based online sportsbook and daily fantasy sports operator, one of the two largest in the US. Its revenue rests on which states legalise betting, how they tax it, and how much bettors lose each weekend.

poly-will-dan-sullivan-win-the-alaska-se.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Dan Sullivan, Alaska's Republican senator since 2015, wins the state's 2026 Senate race. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in cents on the dollar.

stocks:JBLU.standing: The share price of JetBlue Airways, a New York-based US airline built around JFK and Boston, flying domestic, Caribbean and transatlantic routes. Fuel costs and its own debt load weigh on it more than on larger rivals.

poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the ceasefire between the United States and Iran survives to 8 November. Its price is what traders pay for that outcome, and it reacts to Gulf strikes and to talks through mediators.
poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.recent: Vance wrote to Iran's security chief Rezaei and, per Russian state news agency TASS, Iran offered to reopen Hormuz within 2 days of a deal. Limpet mines disabled a tanker there, US officials warned Gulf states of strikes after 3 November, and Khamenei ordered commanders to answer any attack without geographic limits. None of it explains the price.

stocks:TGT.standing: Shares of Target, the Minneapolis-based discount retailer with nearly 2,000 US stores selling groceries, clothing and household goods. Its sales read directly on how much middle-income American households will spend.

stocks:WMT.standing: The world's largest retailer by revenue, running supermarkets and warehouse clubs across the US and abroad. Its sales show what American households at every income level are spending on groceries and essentials.
stocks:WMT.recent: Walmart joined Eli Lilly and 36 other companies objecting to OKX and ICE trading tokenized versions of their shares, a refusal over who controls their shareholder records. It came after the rally and does not account for it; nothing in the input explains the climb.

stocks:WDS.standing: The Australian oil and gas producer behind the North West Shelf and Pluto LNG plants in Western Australia, shown here by its New York listing. Its earnings ride on Asian LNG contracts, most of them priced off oil.
stocks:WDS.recent: QatarEnergy agreed to buy up to 3 million tonnes a year of US liquefied natural gas through a deal with Woodside, turning to American supply as the Hormuz force majeure dragged on. The agreement was reported on 2026-10-29, after the last price on the chart, so it does not account for the move shown.

stocks:LLY.standing: The Indianapolis drugmaker behind the diabetes and obesity drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound. Their sales have made it the world's most valuable pharmaceutical company, so its share price is a running bet on the weight-loss market.
stocks:LLY.recent: Eli Lilly joined Walmart and 36 other companies in objecting to OKX and ICE's plan to trade tokenized versions of their shares. That leaves most of the issuers asked opting out, but nothing in the news accounts for the rise in Lilly's own stock.

stocks:ICE.standing: The company that owns the New York Stock Exchange, the futures market where Brent crude trades, and the clearing houses behind both. Much of its income comes from trading volume, so volatility tends to reach its share.
stocks:ICE.recent: Walmart and Eli Lilly joined 36 other companies objecting to OKX-ICE tokenized versions of their shares, and a majority of issuers opted out. That pushback against a new product does not account for the rise in the stock.

poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if no senior American and Iranian officials meet before 2026 ends. The two governments have met at that level only rarely since 1979, so a meeting would break a long pattern.
poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.recent: Contact this fortnight ran through paper and mediators, not a room: Vance sent a letter to Iran's security chief Rezaei, and TASS reported Araghchi offering to reopen Hormuz within 2 days of a deal. US officials meanwhile warned Gulf states of strikes after 3 November, and Khamenei ordered commanders to answer any attack without geographic limits.

stocks:CG.standing: One of the world's largest private-equity firms, based in Washington, running buyout, credit and infrastructure funds for pensions and endowments. Its earnings swing on the profits it books when it sells what it owns.
stocks:CG.recent: The only news here about Carlyle's own business came on 2026-10-29, after the last close shown: with the EBRD, it is selling Black Sea Oil & Gas, Romania's offshore gas producer, to Mazarine Energy as EU gas tops €100. That sale does not account for the earlier moves in the share.

stocks:SNP.RO.standing: Romania's largest oil and gas producer, listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange and controlled by Austria's OMV, with the Romanian state as a minority holder. It develops the Black Sea's Neptun Deep gas field with Romgaz.

stocks:SNG.RO.standing: Romania's largest natural gas producer, majority-owned by the state and listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange. It owns half of Neptun Deep, the deep-water Black Sea gas project it is developing with OMV Petrom.

stocks:CART.standing: Maplebear is the company behind Instacart, the North American app that sends gig shoppers to pick and deliver groceries from supermarket shelves. It earns from delivery fees and from ads that brands buy inside the app.
stocks:CART.recent: DoorDash agreed to buy Instacart, which would fold the two largest delivery apps into one company and put the gig workers on both under a single employer. A takeover sets a price the buyer will pay for every share, and the stock moves toward it.

stocks:DASH.standing: DoorDash runs the largest food-delivery app in the United States and owns Wolt in Europe. Its share price follows order volume and the rules governing how it pays and dispatches its gig couriers.
stocks:DASH.recent: The one story about DoorDash's own business landed after the chart's last close: on 2026-10-29 it agreed to buy Instacart for $17 billion, putting the largest US restaurant and grocery delivery apps under one owner, with the FTC already probing how such platforms set courier pay. Nothing reported before that accounts for the slide.

stocks:RDDT.standing: Shares of Reddit, the US forum built from thousands of user-run communities, listed on the New York Stock Exchange since 2024. It earns from advertising and from licensing its users' posts to AI companies as training data.
stocks:RDDT.recent: Reddit lost over 1 million weekly search referrals in October as AI answers stopped sending clicks, and Steve Huffman told shareholders the site is moving to logged-in-only access. The wall serves two ends at once: keeping AI scrapers out and selling its data to them, at the cost of the search visitors who arrived without an account.

stocks:RTX.standing: An American aerospace and defence group whose Raytheon unit builds missiles such as the Patriot, and whose Pratt & Whitney engines power airliners and fighters. Its share moves on defence budgets and jet-engine output.

stocks:ABBN.SW.standing: A Zurich-based maker of electrification and automation equipment: switchgear, motors, drives and the control systems that run plants and grids. Its orders track what industry and utilities spend on power infrastructure.

stocks:6954.T.standing: Fanuc Corporation is a Japanese maker of industrial robots and the numerical controllers that run machine tools. Its orders track how much factories worldwide spend on automation, especially carmakers and electronics makers.
stocks:6954.T.recent: Trump set a 180-day clock on foreign robot imports in Washington, the first step toward tariffs on the machines Fanuc sells into American factories. That decision came at the end of the window, and nothing in the input explains the share's earlier fall.

stocks:6506.T.standing: One of the world's largest makers of industrial robots, servo motors and drives, based in Kitakyushu and listed in Tokyo. Its orders are read as an early gauge of factory spending in China and beyond.
stocks:6506.T.recent: Trump set a 180-day clock on foreign robot imports, which bears directly on the robots this company ships into the American market. That move came after the slide, and nothing in the input explains the earlier fall.

stocks:INTC.standing: The American chipmaker that both designs processors and makes them in its own fabs, the largest US bid at leading-edge manufacturing. Its share price answers to Washington's industrial policy as much as to PC and server demand.
stocks:INTC.recent: Intel beat revenue guidance and still plunged after hours on a slump in PC chip sales, with AI spending fears hitting tech at the same time. The drop shaved about $10 billion off the US government's equity stake and dragged down AMD and Arm. A week earlier, Intel won a waiver from the US ban on foreign-made robots, saying no US-made robot fits its fabs.

stocks:CRCL.standing: The company behind USDC, the second-largest dollar stablecoin. It earns most of its revenue from interest on the reserves backing each token, so its shares move with US interest rates and demand for stablecoins.

stocks:ESLT.standing: Israel's largest listed defence contractor, based in Haifa, making drones, artillery, electronic systems and munitions. Its order book follows Israel's own wars and European rearmament, and its share price answers to that backlog.

stocks:GM.standing: The Detroit carmaker behind Chevrolet, GMC, Cadillac and Buick, and one of America's largest by sales. Its profits lean heavily on pickups and SUVs sold in North America, so its shares are exposed to US car demand and trade policy.
stocks:GM.recent: General Motors agreed to pay $220 million after selling data from its Smart Driver system to brokers who passed it to insurers, but that news came after the latest price here and does not account for it. Nothing else in the fortnight's reporting explains the share price.

stocks:4901.T.standing: The Tokyo-listed Japanese group that outlived the collapse of photographic film by moving into healthcare, semiconductor materials and imaging, in one of the best-known corporate reinventions in Japan.
stocks:4901.T.recent: Fujifilm is spending $63 million to quintuple its capacity for magnetic tape, a medium it first made in the 1950s. That report from Odawara is dated after the rise on this chart, so it does not account for the share price.

poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-nebras.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if a Republican wins Nebraska's 2026 US Senate race. The state leans heavily Republican, so any price well short of certainty is money staked on an upset.

stocks:TSAT.standing: A Canadian satellite operator in Ottawa, long a geostationary fleet owner, now building Lightspeed, a low-Earth-orbit network for governments and businesses. Its shares weigh that costly build against the debt on its older satellites.
stocks:TSAT.recent: Telesat owes C$2.4 billion on its legacy geostationary business on 6 December, and its CEO told analysts he is 'pretty constrained' in what he can say about refinancing. That old business is shrinking, while Lightspeed, Canada's bet on a non-Starlink network, depends on the same company.

poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-michigan.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Democratic candidate wins Michigan's 2026 US Senate race, an open seat in a state that swings between parties. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and the seat counts toward Senate control.

poly-will-christine-lagarde-win-the-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Christine Lagarde, a former French finance minister who went on to lead the European Central Bank, wins France's 2027 presidential election. She has never stood for elected office.

poly-2026-senate-map-r-ia-ks.standing: A Polymarket contract on one exact combination of US Senate results: Republicans win Iowa and Kansas but lose Alaska, Maine, Michigan, Ohio and Texas. It pays only if all seven races land that way, and that demands a very specific map.

wiki-united-states-senate.standing: The upper chamber of the US Congress: 100 members, two per state, on six-year terms. It confirms judges and cabinet officers and ratifies treaties, so a one-seat majority can decide whose nominees get through.
wiki-united-states-senate.recent: Alaska's race became the fight: a second Dan Sullivan on the ballot led Trump to demand Peltola's prosecution, the Justice Department sued over certification in a suit that applies only if the Republican loses, and federal agents surged into Alaska days before the vote. In Michigan, Trump called Senate candidate El-Sayed a jihadist.

wiki-china.standing: Daily readings of Wikipedia's article on China, the world's largest exporter and second-largest economy. Its trade, its rivalry with Washington and its disputes with neighbours send readers looking for the country behind the headline.
wiki-china.recent: A magnitude-7 earthquake in Tibet killed 16, by one report, and Kim Jong Un reaffirmed ties with China on a visit to a Chinese border city. New export orders fell to 48.7 while Li Qiang told Steinmeier that China would import more German goods. All of this came weeks after the largest spike, and none of it explains that.

stocks:BIDU.standing: Baidu runs China's dominant search engine and has staked its next chapter on artificial intelligence: its Ernie models, its cloud business and its Apollo Go robotaxis. Its US-listed shares trade on Nasdaq.
stocks:BIDU.recent: The one recent report on Baidu's own business is a product deployment in Wuhan, where its AI agent turns residents' group chats into work orders. It appeared after the shares had already fallen and does not account for the price.

stocks:BABA.standing: The New York-listed shares of China's largest e-commerce group, owner of Taobao and Tmall and the country's biggest cloud provider. The price carries Chinese consumer demand, Beijing's regulation and US-China tension.
stocks:BABA.recent: Apple tapped Alibaba's Qwen for Chinese iPhones, but that news came after the last close on the chart and accounts for none of the fall. Nothing else from these weeks concerns Alibaba's own business.

stocks:1024.HK.standing: Kuaishou runs one of China's largest short-video and livestreaming apps, the main rival to ByteDance's Douyin, and owns the Kling AI video generator. Advertising, livestream tips and e-commerce pay for it.
stocks:1024.HK.recent: Kuaishou's Kling closed a record round, raising 19.8 billion yuan for AI video, but that news arrived only after the last close shown here. Nothing else in the fortnight's reporting accounts for the fall in the shares.

stocks:0268.HK.standing: A Hong Kong-listed Chinese maker of cloud-based accounting and enterprise management software, sold largely to small and mid-sized firms. Its shares are a read on how readily Chinese businesses pay for software subscriptions.

poly-openai-1t-valuation-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, reaches a valuation of at least $1 trillion in 2026. OpenAI is privately held, so this is a rare public wager on what the AI boom's best-known lab is worth.

poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-florida-.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether a Democrat wins Florida's governorship in the November 2026 election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in a state that has elected Republican governors at every contest since 1998.

stocks:BX.standing: One of the world's largest alternative asset managers, investing pension and endowment money in private equity, real estate and private credit. Its share price rises and falls with deal activity, asset sales and the fees those funds earn.

poly-moodys-or-sp-downgrades-france-by-n.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Moody's or S&P cuts France's sovereign credit rating before its deadline. Those ratings feed into what Paris pays to borrow and which funds can hold its bonds.

poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-dem.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Kamala Harris, the former US vice-president, becomes the Democratic presidential candidate in 2028. The price is what traders pay for that outcome, in a race with no votes cast until the primaries open.

poly-will-ron-desantis-win-the-2028-repu.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Florida governor Ron DeSantis becomes the Republican presidential candidate in 2028. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it sets him against the rest of the party's post-Trump field.

stocks:LMT.standing: The world's largest defence contractor, maker of the F-35 fighter and Patriot interceptor missiles. The US government is its main customer, so its shares turn on Pentagon budgets, weapons orders and allied rearmament.
stocks:LMT.recent: Lockheed and the Pentagon struck an initial deal to produce 850 F-35 jets, reported on Oct 22. It is the one development here about the company's own business, and no report ties the share price to it directly.

stocks:AMGN.standing: A large US biotech company living on established medicines for bone loss, cancer and inflammation. Its share turns on patent expiries on those older drugs and on the pipeline meant to replace them.
stocks:AMGN.recent: The FDA moved to withdraw its approval of Tavneos, Amgen's vasculitis drug, saying the approval rested on manipulated data. That news arrived after the share's climb, so it does not account for the rise, and no other report about the company's business explains it.

poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-us-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Kamala Harris, the Democrats' 2024 nominee, wins the 2028 US presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it reacts to moves in the party's nominating contest.

wiki-france.standing: A daily count of people reading Wikipedia's article on France, a nuclear-armed EU member and permanent UN Security Council seat. It shows when the country sends people looking for background, not whether the news there is good or bad.
wiki-france.recent: School protests in France grew into a wider political crisis: partial curfews followed 2,400 arrests, and Macron rejected his interior minister's resignation. Riots returned for a third weekend with more than 500 arrests, while the 10-year bond yield reached 4.96% and Fitch cut its outlook after the economy shrank 0.1%.

poly-will-anthropic-ipo-by-november-30-2.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic, the AI lab behind Claude, goes public by the deadline. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in cents on the dollar.

poly-will-gyanesh-kumar-be-out-as-chief-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Gyanesh Kumar leaves office as India's Chief Election Commissioner by the deadline. The post runs national and state votes, and removal requires the same process as for a Supreme Court judge.
poly-will-gyanesh-kumar-be-out-as-chief-.recent: In Patna, Kharge targeted the election commissioner, saying voter-roll revisions stole 4 state governments. That is an accusation, not a move to oust Gyanesh Kumar, and nothing else from the fortnight accounts for the price.

stocks:2317.TW.standing: Hon Hai, trading as Foxconn, is the Taiwanese contract manufacturer that assembles most of the world's iPhones and a growing share of AI servers. Its share price is a read on demand from Apple and the large data-centre builders.

stocks:ZURN.SW.standing: Zurich Insurance is a Swiss insurer selling property, casualty and life cover worldwide, with a large North American commercial book through Farmers ties. Its profits turn on catastrophe claims, pricing cycles and investment returns on premiums.

poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-iowa-sen.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether a Democrat wins Iowa's US Senate seat in the November 2026 election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in a state that has leaned Republican in recent federal races.

poly-will-spacex-have-the-highest-ipo-ma.standing: The price traders pay on Polymarket for a bet that SpaceX, Elon Musk's rocket and Starlink satellite company, has the highest market value of any 2026 stock-market debut. A listing that size would test how much new stock public markets can absorb.

poly-france-declares-state-of-emergency-.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether France declares a state of emergency. The 1955 law behind it lets the government impose curfews, ban gatherings and order house searches, and was used in the 2005 riots and after the 2015 Paris attacks.

wiki-democratic-party-united-states.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the Democratic Party, one of the two parties that have dominated US politics since the 1850s. Its elections, leaders and fights in Congress send people looking up what the party is.
wiki-democratic-party-united-states.recent: The closing midterm fight ran through Alaska, where the Justice Department sued to block Senate certification only if the Republican loses, and Michigan, where Trump called Senate candidate El-Sayed a jihadist. In Cleveland, Obama blamed the Iran war for rising diesel prices. None of these stories explains the early-October peak.

poly-will-syria-join-the-mecca-agreement.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Syria joins the Mecca Agreement, a regional defence pact, within the contract's 2026 deadline. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it tracks Damascus's alignment with the pact's members.

poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-texas-.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Republican candidate wins the Texas governor's race in 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in a state whose governorship carries weight on border policy and energy.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-win-the-n.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether a Democrat wins North Carolina's 13th congressional district, a U.S. House seat, at the November midterm. The price is what traders pay for that outcome, and it settles once the seat is called.

poly-will-iliana-iotova-win-the-next-bul.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Iliana Iotova, long Rumen Radev's vice-president, wins Bulgaria's election. The presidency is largely ceremonial, but it names caretaker governments, which matters in a country of repeated snap elections.

stocks:MDA.TO.standing: A Canadian space company that builds satellite systems, antennas and robotics, including the Canadarm arms flown on the Space Shuttle and the International Space Station. Its shares turn on large constellation contracts.
stocks:MDA.TO.recent: MDA Space agreed with Thales Alenia Space to build digital antennas for the first 66 satellites of IRIS2, the EU's secure connectivity constellation, under a €64 million deal announced on 30 October, as Canada and the EU explore Canadian participation. The deal came after the share's slide and does not account for it.

poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-republic.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if JD Vance, the US vice president, wins the Republican presidential nomination in 2028. Its price is what bettors will pay for that outcome, and the vice presidency makes him the early name to beat.

stocks:RIO.standing: One of the world's largest miners, listed in London and Sydney and traded in New York through depositary shares. Iron ore from Australia's Pilbara drives its earnings, which ties the share closely to Chinese steel demand.
stocks:RIO.recent: Rio Tinto's Oyu Tolgoi copper mine halted underground operations late in October, the one development in this material about the company's own business. It arrived only in the final days of the decline, so it does not account for the weeks of selling before it.

stocks:BHP.standing: An Anglo-Australian miner and one of the world's largest, listed in New York through American depositary receipts. Iron ore and copper drive its earnings, so its shares carry exposure to Chinese steel demand and global industrial activity.

stocks:NWSA.standing: Owner of The Wall Street Journal, The Times of London, HarperCollins books and a controlling stake in Australia's REA Group. Its value rests on Dow Jones subscriptions and property listings more than on newspaper sales.
stocks:NWSA.recent: A judge in Miami dismissed Trump's defamation suit against the company's Wall Street Journal and ruled that he cannot refile it. The ruling was reported after the last close on this chart, so it accounts for none of the price, and nothing else in the fortnight's news explains the share's move.
